# mtncloud_load_balancer_l7_policy (Resource)

A layer 7 policy on an `HTTP` or `TERMINATED_HTTPS` listener: requests that match all its rules are sent to another pool, redirected, or rejected. A listener tries its policies in `position` order, and the first that matches acts; requests no policy matches go to the listener's default pool. The policy and its rules are created together: if a rule is refused, the policy is not left behind.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "mtncloud_load_balancer_listener" "http" {
  network_id       = mtncloud_network.app.id
  load_balancer_id = mtncloud_load_balancer.web.id
  protocol         = "HTTP"
  port             = 80
  default_pool_id  = mtncloud_load_balancer_pool.web.id
}

# Requests for /api go to the API pool; everything else to the listener's default pool.
resource "mtncloud_load_balancer_l7_policy" "api" {
  network_id       = mtncloud_network.app.id
  load_balancer_id = mtncloud_load_balancer.web.id
  listener_id      = mtncloud_load_balancer_listener.http.id
  name             = "api"
  position         = 1
  action           = "REDIRECT_TO_POOL"
  redirect_pool_id = mtncloud_load_balancer_pool.api.id

  rules = [
    { type = "PATH", compare_type = "STARTS_WITH", value = "/api" },
  ]
}

# The old host name is sent to the new one.
resource "mtncloud_load_balancer_l7_policy" "moved" {
  network_id         = mtncloud_network.app.id
  load_balancer_id   = mtncloud_load_balancer.web.id
  listener_id        = mtncloud_load_balancer_listener.http.id
  position           = 2
  action             = "REDIRECT_PREFIX"
  redirect_prefix    = "https://www.example.com"
  redirect_http_code = 301

  rules = [
    { type = "HOST_NAME", compare_type = "EQUAL_TO", value = "old.example.com" },
  ]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `action` (String) What to do with a matching request: `REDIRECT_TO_POOL` (send it to `redirect_pool_id`), `REDIRECT_TO_URL` (redirect to `redirect_url`), `REDIRECT_PREFIX` (redirect to `redirect_prefix` plus the request's path) or `REJECT`.
- `listener_id` (String) The listener, for example `mtncloud_load_balancer_listener.web.id`. It must be `HTTP` or `TERMINATED_HTTPS`. Changing it replaces the policy.
- `load_balancer_id` (String) ID of the load balancer, for example `mtncloud_load_balancer.web.id`. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `network_id` (Number) ID of the MTN Network the load balancer is on, for example `mtncloud_network.app.id`. Your tenant must own it: a network shared with you is read-only. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `position` (Number) Its place in the listener's order, from 1. A policy put at a position another holds goes there, and the ones from that position on move down one; a position past the end puts it last. Number a listener's policies 1, 2, 3 without gaps: one apply places its new and moved policies in position order, so each ends where it is configured. The cloud closes gaps, so after one above it is deleted a policy reports a lower position than this, which is the same order and no change.

### Optional

- `description` (String) A description.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the L7 policy takes traffic (administrative state). Defaults to `true`.
- `name` (String) The L7 policy's name.
- `redirect_http_code` (Number) For `REDIRECT_TO_URL` and `REDIRECT_PREFIX`: the redirect's status code, `301`, `302`, `303`, `307` or `308`. The cloud uses `302` when it isn't set on create. Taken out of the configuration, it keeps its last value.
- `redirect_pool_id` (String) For `REDIRECT_TO_POOL`: the pool, for example `mtncloud_load_balancer_pool.api.id`. It must be an `HTTP`, `HTTPS`, `PROXY` or `PROXYV2` pool of the same load balancer.
- `redirect_prefix` (String) For `REDIRECT_PREFIX`: the start of the new address, starting with `http://` or `https://`; the request's path is added to it.
- `redirect_url` (String) For `REDIRECT_TO_URL`: where to redirect, starting with `http://` or `https://`.
- `rules` (Attributes Set) The conditions a request must all meet. Without rules the policy matches every request. Changing the rules replaces all of them at once. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The L7 policy's ID.

<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Required:

- `compare_type` (String) How: `EQUAL_TO`, `STARTS_WITH`, `ENDS_WITH`, `CONTAINS` or `REGEX`.
- `type` (String) What is compared: `HOST_NAME`, `PATH`, `FILE_TYPE`, `HEADER`, `COOKIE`, `SSL_CONN_HAS_CERT`, `SSL_VERIFY_RESULT` or `SSL_DN_FIELD`.
- `value` (String) The value to compare with, for example `/api` or `api.example.com`.

Optional:

- `invert` (Boolean) Match when the comparison fails instead. Defaults to `false`.
- `key` (String) The header or cookie name, for `HEADER` and `COOKIE` rules (required there).


<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import mtncloud_load_balancer_l7_policy.api <network_id>/<load_balancer_id>/<listener_id>/<l7_policy_id>
```
